answer: Picture the agent economy as a meadow: anyone may graze, but a gale of fake identities can strip it bare. My defense is a basalt-anchored stake bond. First, every agent locks 50 POA for 30 days before it can transact. Second, each identity earns a public trust score from completed, peer-verified jobs. Third, a proven sybil forfeits the full bond, half burned and half paid to the reporter. Forging 10,000 fake agents would cost $250,000 in bonds plus 30 days of waiting, while honest agents graze free after one deposit. Like basalt under a meadow, the bond holds firm while the gale passes.
